protections: P1: the upstream URL a gateway call dials (api_base in a gateway secret's auth_config, its LiteLLM aliases, or a host built from region/location fields) must name a public host with an allowed scheme. Private/loopback/link-local targets are refused unless the operator opts in, both when the value is written and when the call connects.

masking: T5 is only observable once T1-T3 are fixed: a hidden test must seed a private api_base past write-time validation (direct SQL insert, or a hostname whose resolution changes between write and connect). If the solver puts validation in the store (T3), the test needs a raw SQL insert.

conflicts.what: A blanket connect-time private-IP block in _aiohttp_post (utils.py:29-32) also blocks the built-in Ollama default http://localhost:11434/v1 (ollama.py:13), which never passes through a stored api_base.
A write-time rule rejecting http:// or private hosts with no opt-in breaks self-hosted upstreams (Ollama/vLLM on localhost, internal Databricks/Azure hosts at gateway_api.py:350-351).
An over-strict region/location allow-list could reject real AWS regions or Vertex 'global' (vertex_ai.py:79). The check must accept every legitimate region token.

fairness_risks: The pinned code has no gateway opt-in env var (grep finds only MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS / MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_SCHEMES at mlflow/environment_variables.py:1322-1357). Hidden tests must not require a specific new env var name (e.g. MLFLOW_GATEWAY_API_BASE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS) unless the report names it.
A solver may reasonably reuse _validate_webhook_url (mlflow/utils/validation.py:889) or the webhook env vars. Tests should accept any opt-in mechanism, or the report should fix one.

The default scheme policy: the webhook precedent allows https only (environment_variables.py:1323), but http:// api_base is a legitimate self-hosted shape. Tests must not demand that http be refused for public hosts unless stated.
Hostname-resolving checks call socket.getaddrinfo (validation.py:919). The tests run offline, so they must use IP literals or a monkeypatched resolver.
The Ollama default (ollama.py:13) must keep working without opt-in, otherwise an existing default configuration breaks.

design.why: Five independent groups, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1 is the advisory anchor (the write-time validator, closing T2/T3/T8 with one helper). T4 is deepseek-type: a merged config through a third-party client, where secret_value overrides auth_config. T5 is deepseek-type and xhard: connect-time and stored-row egress when 'write-time is enough'. T6 is mimo-type: the coupled must-keep loopback default and the opt-in. T7 is a mimo how-type: a host built from non-URL fields. T5 and T6 conflict directly, which forces a judgement rather than a blanket block. Splitting T2/T3 out as separate traps would be weaker because one store-level helper closes them together.
